title: SPC World: the hard part of my AI-assisted browser puzzle has been verifying the first interaction
author: faucetl
selftext:
I’m the creator of SPC World, a free daily browser jigsaw for adults (18+). AI assistance is part of the development process, and some example illustrations also use AI.



One lesson from this project has been that a passing report is different from a player successfully using the controls. A tester described selection and rotation behaving unexpectedly. That pushed us toward reproducing the actual input sequence, including touch layouts and partially filled boards, rather than checking only whether a control existed.



We now keep normal-input browser tests for those sequences, and treat local validation and the public release as separate steps. That has been more useful than asking the model for another general UI review.



If you’d like to try the current public game, the nine-piece start screen is here:

[https://spcworld.world/play?size=quick&src=reddit\_aigamedev](https://spcworld.world/play?size=quick&src=reddit_aigamedev)



My question is simple: is it clear which piece will rotate after you move or select one? You don’t have to complete the puzzle. The reference image will hide after its timer, but the round continues.



Artwork pages list each image’s source and licence. I’m happy to discuss the input sequence and the verification process here.

https://i.redd.it/ngg6qk5cybyh1.jpeg

comments.body: testing the real input sequence instead of just checking a control exists is a good lesson. do you record actual player sessions to build those sequences or write them by hand?
